taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Court-road, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 16.8 | 2.56 | 2.56
2 | 73.3 | 10.4 | 12.9
3 | 701 | 49.9 | 62.9
4 | 51.6 | 51.4 | 114
5 | 99.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AKH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Court-road, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station Court-road, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation yields a 5-layer model: a thin resistive-to-conductive surface layer (16.8 Ω·m, 2.56 m), underlain by a moderately resistive layer (73.3 Ω·m, 10.4 m to 12.9 m depth), a highly resistive layer (701 Ω·m, extending to 62.9 m), a lower-resistivity layer (51.6 Ω·m, to 114 m depth), and a resistive basal layer (99.8 Ω·m, inferred infinite thickness).

Applying the curve-type convention to the resistivity sequence (16.8–73.3–701–51.6–99.8):
- Layers 1-2-3: increasing → A
- Layers 2-3-4: increase then decrease → K
- Layers 3-4-5: decrease then increase → H

This gives curve type AKH, consistent with the on-file classification. No discrepancy is noted between the computed curve type and the filed label.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKH", "label_issue_flagged": false}
